note: Both streets slanted. Water-pipe lines run inside both streets and one joins the Kentucky south side; taken as pipes, not block lines. Carlin legs north and south line up.

The two streets do not meet in 1922. Lambston comes up from lower-left, turns north near (500,3600) as a 25 ft strip and dead-ends near (520,3425). Washburn ends at Carlin near (698,3572). Lots 37, 45-48 lie between them.

T: Washburn ends at Carlin from the east. East edge of Carlin north of Washburn and north edge of Washburn are hard to separate from a water-pipe line and a grey colour band; could be off by 10-15 px.

Identity doubtful. Point is where narrow Lambston ends (T) at the wide diagonal street along the plate edge, which looks like Colerain (car-track dashes, 4in pipe), unnamed in this piece; its far side is cut by the plate edge so the centre is estimated. It is about 185 px from the image middle. The street printed LEEPER ST./CHASE in the next crop starts near (505,4005) and does not reach Lambston. Another street printed LEEPER S(T) runs NNE at upper left.

No cross street drawn here: lots are continuous on both sides of Leeper St./Chase (street widens 30 ft to 50 ft near (780,4260), name changes Leeper to Chase). The only side street off Chase is the unnamed 40 ft strip at about (973,4425), reported as 45-008, far in the lower-right corner of this piece.
Four-way; north and south legs of the up-down street line up, no jog. Washburn slants down to the right.

Not a crossing but a bend: Badgly St. coming down from the north turns south-west at a subdivision boundary (colour bands) and continues as an unnamed 40 ft strip with a 4in water pipe down to Chase. Point is where the two centre lines meet at the bend.
T: unnamed 40 ft strip (continuation of Badgly St., 4in water pipe in it) ends at the north-east side of Chase between lots 113 and 13. Nothing continues south-west of Chase.

Jog. Used the eastern, left-right leg (unnamed here, 42in sewer, runs east from Virginia). The western leg, printed AVE. (Chase) and running upper-left to lower-right, meets Virginia's centre line further south-west at about (1320,4749). Heavy pipe and track linework at the junction.
T: the up-down street ends at the left-right street from the south; a large unsubdivided lot (304.96 ft) is on the north side. Left-right street carries a 42in sewer.
T: Robley ends at Kirby from the west. Kirby is slanted (upper-left to lower-right); its east edge is the thin Krismer property line.
No street on the east side of Kirby in 1922: open tract lettered ROSE KRISMER. Only Robley meets Kirby here (see 45-011, about 2580,614).
No street running lower-left to upper-right off Kirby is drawn; east of Kirby is the open ROSE KRISMER tract. Only Robley (left-right, from the west) meets Kirby in this piece.

T: the up-down street (slanted, 6in water pipe in it, hydrant at the corner) ends at the left-right street from the south; Squires tract on the north side. The left-right street is narrow (about 40 px) and has sewer lettering only.
No up-down street drawn: north side is the C.F. McClure tract (lot 184) bounded by single property lines, south side is continuous lots 51, 52, 80-85.
T: the left-right street (unnamed in this piece, 60 marked, dashed sewer in it) ends at the slanted up-down street from the east; lots are continuous on the west side.

No up-down street here in 1922: open land on both sides of Bruce. The only up-down line is a long dashed 149in sewer crossing Bruce near (2335,3310), not a street. Nearest real side street is the 50 ft AVE. at about (2681,3361), outside this piece's target area.

No street within about 150 px of the middle. A 50 ft street printed ...AVE. runs south from Bruce (T, nothing north) at about (2681,3361), roughly 190 px east of the middle; cannot tell whether it is Georgia Court, Georgia Avenue or the next street east, so not recorded.
